card.name: Small words after 'basis' or 'causes'
card.fires_on: The words 'for' or 'of' right after an abstract noun like 'basis' or 'causes', at the start of a clause beginning with 'Although' or 'While'. It appears in trial-result passages comparing drug and placebo rates.

modes.label: 'of' after causes
modes.description: The word 'of' following 'causes' in a sentence about deaths in a drug versus placebo comparison.
modes.example: in drug-treated patients was about 4.5%, compared to a rate of about 2.6% in the placebo group. Although the causes<< of>> death were varied, most of the deaths

modes.label: 'for' after basis
modes.description: The word 'for' following 'basis' in a concessive clause about a reported difference in rates.
modes.example: 0.7% (5/687) of placebo-treated patients. While the basis<< for>> the reported difference in seizure rate is not
